bullets: Game 2 of 7 in a single-deck showcase video ("Playing the 8 BEST Cards in a SINGLE Deck"); the same eight cards are the video-level consensus across all seven games, with evolution slots on Elite Barbarians and Battle Ram.

Piloted as bridge spam and named as such at overtime 0:28 — "I just have to keep on bridge spamming this guy." Elite Barbarians, Battle Ram and Goblinstein are cycled at the bridge in alternating lanes ((3, 13) and (14, 13) Ebarbs, (2, 14)/(16, 15)/(3, 14)/(15, 15) Battle Ram, (2, 13)/(4, 15)/(14, 13) Goblinstein) with Mother Witch and Cannon Cart placed one row back down the middle as support.

The deck has no reliable defensive building, so defence is Heal Spirit chip, Zap, Barbarian Barrel and whatever Goblinstein/Cannon Cart is already on the field; against X-Bow siege that meant conceding 1083 HP off the right tower and 235 off the left over regular time while never losing a tower.

Evolution management drives the sequencing: two six/four-elixir cards are played from the back purely to cycle ("split Earbs in the back here just to get to my EVO" at 1:43, Battle Ram at the bridge at 2:09 "just to get to the evo"), and Ryley tracks the opponent's evolution counter in parallel ("he's going to be one Tesla away from EVO, too", 1:09).

Result: a win on the overtime tiebreaker. He was "only behind by six damage" at overtime 1:01 (own right 4050 vs enemy left 4056), took the enemy left tower to 4056 with a Battle Ram + Goblinstein + Zap + Heal Spirit push at overtime 1:13-1:07, then flooded the right bridge in the last twenty seconds to drop the enemy right tower 4704 -> 3451 below his own lowest (3775). "Give us one. Give us one. Yes. Let's go. Oh my god. What a win, man. We barely grabbed that."

new_deck.rationale: Three separate bridge threats (Evo Elite Barbarians, Evo Battle Ram, Goblinstein) cycled in alternating lanes with no building and no beatdown tank, and Ryley describes the plan himself as "bridge spamming this guy".
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck wins by never letting the defender settle: Evo Elite Barbarians, Evo Battle Ram and Goblinstein are all playable at the bridge for 4-6 elixir, so at double and triple elixir Ryley can present a new threat in a fresh lane roughly every four seconds while Cannon Cart and Mother Witch trail one row behind as support. Goblinstein is the glue — placed centrally it splits the Doctor and Monster into both lanes, placed at the bridge its Lightning Link clears the ranged support ("we can grab the one evo archer off of the board") that would otherwise stop the ram. Heal Spirit and Zap are the whole defensive and cycle budget, which makes the deck fragile against siege chip but very fast to re-arm; against X-Bow the plan is explicitly to out-tempo a defender whose rotation cannot answer a Cannon Cart ("he has no knight and cycle so he's unable to block a cannon cart on the expo"). Its weakness shows in the same game: with no defensive building Ryley conceded over 1000 HP off one tower and had to win the match on a last-twenty-second tower race.
